retrieval_note: Not a data source. This fixture records the retrieval environment so a later reviewer can distinguish 'the figure is wrong' from 'the figure could not be read'. Recorded because GATE-ORF produced ZERO successful direct retrievals of any primary source. source_type is set to primary_government only to satisfy the schema enumeration; this is diagnostic infrastructure, not evidence about any drug.

class_1_egress_policy_denial.mechanism: gateway answered 403 to CONNECT; recorded in proxy recentRelayFailures
class_1_egress_policy_denial.note: Some of these hosts were requested by sibling agents sharing this proxy, not by GATE-ORF. api.fda.gov was requested by GATE-ORF and denied.

class_2_origin_bot_block.mechanism: CONNECT tunnel succeeded (no relay failure recorded), origin returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to the fetcher

extracted.bash_curl_status: curl from Bash was denied at the gateway for www.sec.gov, www.fda.gov and www.lilly.com (CONNECT 403), so no User-Agent accommodation could be applied even where the origin would have accepted one.
extracted.tos_and_robots: robots.txt could not be retrieved for sec.gov, fda.gov or lilly.com (gateway denial), so programmatic-access permissions are recorded as unclear rather than assumed.
extracted.net_effect: Zero primary sources were directly readable. All substantive content in GATE-ORF was surfaced only through the WebSearch tool's summarizer. Under the gate's rules of evidence, no dollar figure may be marked confirmed.

verbatim_excerpt: Proxy status, quoted verbatim: "kind": "connect_rejected", "detail": "gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)", "host": "api.fda.gov:443". WebFetch, quoted verbatim for every primary URL attempted: "The server returned HTTP 403 Forbidden."
